prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Scottish National Party Manifesto 2015 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core aim
- Make Scotland stronger at Westminster with a louder, progressive voice. Oppose austerity, protect public services, and never put the Tories into power; work with others to lock them out if there’s an anti‑Tory majority and push Labour to deliver real change.

Economy and public finances
- End austerity with modest, responsible spending increases each year; focus on infrastructure to boost jobs, productivity and growth, while reducing deficit and debt as a share of GDP.
- Fairer taxation: restore 50p top rate; bank levy and bankers’ bonus tax; mansion tax; abolish non‑dom status; reverse married couples’ allowance; crack down on avoidance. Create a Sovereign Wealth/Energy Fund when conditions allow.

Jobs, business and investment
- Minimum wage to £8.70 by 2020; expand Living Wage.
- Seed‑fund a Scottish Business Development Bank; strengthen export finance; legal protections for small firms against late payment; raise Employment Allowance to £6,000 by 2019‑20.
- Devolve and cut Air Passenger Duty by 50% (abolish over time); explore VAT cut for hospitality.
- Major infrastructure: connect Scotland to HS2 (build north and south), invest in northern transport and broadband/4G with a Universal Service Obligation; UK target of 100,000 affordable homes a year.
- Creative sector: fairer BBC Scotland share (+£100m), retain Video Games tax relief, establish a Creative Content Fund.

Welfare, work and equality
- Scrap the Bedroom Tax; halt Universal Credit and PIP rollouts, reverse DLA→PIP; uprate benefits at least by cost of living; raise UC work allowance by 20%.
- Reform sanctions and Work Capability Assessments; curb exploitative zero‑hours contracts.
- Carer’s Allowance up to JSA level (+~£600/yr); protect ILF; no HB restrictions for 18–21s; war disablement pensions disregarded in means‑tests.
- Equalities: commence Equal Pay audits (Equality Act s.78); 50% women on public boards; tougher action on maternity discrimination; abolish VAT on sanitary products; keep Human Rights Act and ECHR; review immigration detention.

NHS and public services
- Increase UK health spending by £24bn above inflation by 2020‑21, delivering £2bn extra for NHS Scotland; protect NHS from privatisation; expand mental health funding to £100m.
- 30 hours/week free childcare for all 3–4s and eligible 2‑year‑olds; 30,000 Modern Apprenticeships; free university tuition maintained.

Energy, climate and bills
- Cut bills by shifting ECO to general taxation and forcing pass‑through of wholesale price falls (~£100/household).
- Strong renewables (offshore, onshore, hydro, CCS), island interconnectors, reformed transmission charging; expand community energy; maintain fracking moratorium; establish a Climate Justice Fund.

Defence and security
- Oppose Trident renewal (save up to £100bn lifetime); procure Maritime Patrol Aircraft and patrol vessels in Scotland; build Type 26 in Scotland; greater MOD transparency; better support for service personnel. Oppose mass surveillance (“snoopers’ charter”); back targeted, overseen measures.

Rural, seas and communities
- Fair share of CAP convergence uplift; workable discard ban; devolve Crown Estate seabed revenues to coastal communities; fair rural fuel pricing; reinstate west‑coast towing vessel; return ARCC to Kinloss. Protect Royal Mail USO; aim to return Royal Mail to public ownership.

Europe and world
- Oppose Brexit; require a UK‑wide “double majority” by nation; stronger devolved role in EU; exempt NHS/Scottish Water from TTIP; support EAW.
- Back 0.7% aid (no defence use); recognise Palestine; create an LGBTI rights envoy.

Democracy and devolution
- Reform Westminster: STV for elections, abolish House of Lords, votes at 16–17, robust MP recall, fair lobbying rules.
- Deliver Smith Commission in full, then move to full fiscal responsibility; prioritise devolution of welfare, employment (incl. minimum wage), business taxes, NICs, equality, broadcasting, gambling/payday lending powers.
- SNP MPs will oppose any Westminster measure that reduces Scotland’s funding.
